alt: Place-value grid for the binary number 11010110: the 1s are under 128, 64, 16, 4 and 2, and 128 + 64 + 16 + 4 + 2 = 214; the places holding 0 add nothing
caption: Figure: converting 11010110 to denary by adding the place values that hold a 1

alt: Bubble sort of 27, 12, 35, 8, 19: pass 1 makes 3 swaps and moves 35 to the end giving 12, 27, 8, 19, 35; pass 2 gives 12, 8, 19, 27, 35; pass 3 gives 8, 12, 19, 27, 35 and pass 4 makes no swaps
caption: Figure: the first pass of a bubble sort comparison by comparison, then the array after each later pass

alt: Circuit for X = ((NOT A) AND B) OR (B NOR C): A goes through NOT then AND with B to give P, B and C enter a NOR gate to give Q, and P and Q enter an OR gate that gives X
caption: Figure: the circuit for X = ((NOT A) AND B) OR (B NOR C)

alt: Data flow diagram of a library loan system: the Learner sends Learner ID and book to process 1 Record loan, which reads book details from store D1 Books, saves loan details in D2 Loans and returns a return date; process 2 reads overdue loans from D2 Loans and sends an overdue list to the Librarian
caption: Figure: a data flow diagram with two entities, two processes and two data stores

alt: How a web page is retrieved: the browser sends the domain name to a DNS server, which returns the IP address; the browser then sends a request to the web server at that IP address, the server returns HTML and images, and the browser renders them
caption: Figure: the seven steps from typing a URL to seeing the page

alt: Symmetric encryption uses one shared key (MEET AT NOON becomes PHHW DW QRRQ with key 3, and the same key decrypts it); asymmetric encryption uses the receiver's public key to encrypt and the matching private key, which never leaves the receiver, to decrypt
caption: Figure: symmetric encryption with one shared key and asymmetric encryption with a public and private key

alt: Entity-relationship diagram in crow's foot notation: Borrower and Book each link to Loan with a plain end (one) at Borrower or Book and a crow's foot (many) at Loan; Loan holds BorrowerID and BookID as foreign keys, so it resolves the many-to-many link
caption: Figure: an ERD for a school library with Loan as the link table

alt: Fetch-decode-execute cycle: fetch copies the PC to the MAR, reads the instruction into the MDR, adds 1 to the PC and copies the instruction to the CIR; decode is done by the control unit; execute fetches any data and the ALU stores its result in the ACC; then the cycle repeats
caption: Figure: the fetch-decode-execute cycle as three repeating stages

alt: Flowchart of a loop that adds numbers until the rogue value -1: the decision Number = -1 comes straight after each input, so -1 is never added; with inputs 6, 9, 4, -1 the output is 19 3
caption: Figure: a flowchart loop that totals numbers until the rogue value -1 is entered

alt: Flowchart for the game park fee: input Age; if Age < 12 the fee is 2; otherwise if Age >= 60 the fee is 3; otherwise the fee is 5; then output the fee. Ages 9, 35 and 60 give 2, 5 and 3
caption: Figure: the game park fee flowchart with two decision boxes

alt: Hexadecimal 3F9C converts to binary by replacing each hex digit with its 4-bit nibble: 3 is 0011, F is 1111, 9 is 1001 and C is 1100, giving 0011111110011100
caption: Figure: 3F9C written as four nibbles of binary

alt: Input, process, output and storage: a barcode scanner sends input to the CPU (control unit directs, ALU calculates), which exchanges instructions and data with main memory, sends results to the screen and printer, and main memory loads from and saves to the SSD or hard disk
caption: Figure: input, processing (CPU and main memory), output and storage at a supermarket till

alt: Two linked tables: Doctors has primary key DoctorID (D1, D2, D3); Patients has primary key PatientID and a foreign key DoctorID, which repeats (D2 appears three times) and leads each patient to one doctor, for example Farai Zhou's D3 leads to Dr Gumbo
caption: Figure: primary keys and a foreign key linking the Patients table to the Doctors table

alt: Path of a web page request from a school computer: the NIC sends packets, the switch uses the MAC address to pass them only to the router, the router uses the IP address to forward them towards the ISP, and a modem converts the signal if the line is analogue
caption: Figure: the devices a web request passes through, from computer to internet

alt: Linear search of the codes 418, 205, 377, 960, 122, 543, 381, 709: searching for 122 stops at index 5 after 5 comparisons, while searching for 300 compares all 8 codes and reports Not found
caption: Figure: a linear search finding 122 at index 5, and failing to find 300 after 8 comparisons

alt: The six logic gate symbols with the output pattern each gives for inputs 00, 01, 10, 11: NOT 10, AND 0001, OR 0111, NAND 1110, NOR 1000, XOR 0110; a bubble at the output means invert
caption: Figure: the six gate symbols and the output pattern each gives (a bubble means invert)

alt: Four topologies with five computers each: star (5 cables to a central switch), bus (one backbone with a terminator at each end), ring (each computer linked to two neighbours, data in one direction) and full mesh (every pair linked, 10 cables)
caption: Figure: star, bus, ring and full mesh topologies for five computers

alt: A 3,000-byte file is split into 3 packets of 1,000 bytes; each packet has a header (destination address, originator address, packet number), a payload of data and a trailer (end marker and error check)
caption: Figure: three packets from one file, each with a header, a payload and a trailer

alt: Packet switching: packets 1, 2 and 4 travel via the Masvingo router and packet 3 via Mutare because the Masvingo link is busy, so they arrive in the order 1, 2, 4, 3 and the receiver sorts them by packet number into 1, 2, 3, 4
caption: Figure: packets taking different routes, arriving out of order and being put back in order

alt: Even-parity block of four bytes and a parity byte: byte 3 has five 1s and column 4 has three 1s, both odd, so the bit where they cross (byte 3, column 4) is the error and should be 0
caption: Figure: the parity block, with the failing row and column crossing at the wrong bit

alt: Payback period graph: cumulative net savings of USD 6,000 a year (7,000 saving less 1,000 running cost) rise to meet the USD 12,000 development cost after 2 years, and reach USD 30,000 by year 5
caption: Figure: cumulative net savings against the 12,000 development cost, meeting at 2 years

alt: The four stages of the program development life cycle in a cycle: analysis, design, coding, testing; testing leads back to analysis or design when a fault or a misunderstood requirement is found
caption: Figure: the program development life cycle as a repeating cycle of four stages

alt: Monitoring and control: a sensor's reading goes through an ADC to the microprocessor, which compares it with stored limits; in monitoring it only warns a person, in control it also signals an actuator whose effect on the conditions is read again by the sensor, forming a feedback loop
caption: Figure: sensor, ADC, microprocessor and actuator in a control loop, with the monitoring branch

alt: Serial sends the byte 01001011 as eight bits one after another along one wire; parallel sends the same eight bits at once along eight wires, one bit per wire
caption: Figure: the byte 01001011 sent serially (one wire) and in parallel (eight wires)

alt: Grain silo alarm circuit X = (A AND B) OR C: A and B enter an AND gate, its output and C enter an OR gate, so the alarm sounds if temperature is high and the fan has failed, or the button is pressed
caption: Figure: the grain silo alarm circuit, X = (A AND B) OR C

alt: SQL query stages on Rudo's plants table: WHERE Type = 'Herb' keeps Basil, Rosemary and Mint; ORDER BY Price DESC puts Rosemary (4), Basil (3), Mint (2) in that order; SELECT PlantName, Price shows only those two fields
caption: Figure: a query filters with WHERE, sorts with ORDER BY, then shows only the SELECT fields

alt: Structure diagram of a library loans system: the top box splits into Manage members (Add member, Remove member), Manage loans (Issue book, Return book, Calculate fine) and Produce reports
caption: Figure: a top-down structure diagram for a library loans system

alt: System flowchart for bus bookings: the clerk's manual input goes to Validate and check seat, which reads the Bookings file; if the seat is taken the screen shows Seat already booked, if free the booking is saved to the file and a ticket is printed
caption: Figure: a system flowchart using the manual input, process, disk, display and document symbols

alt: TCP/IP has four layers (application, transport, internet, link) lined up against the seven OSI layers: application covers OSI 5 to 7, transport is layer 4, internet is layer 3 and link covers layers 1 and 2; a hub works at physical, a switch at data link, a router at network
caption: Figure: the four TCP/IP layers against the seven OSI layers, with the layer each device works at

alt: Simplex sends data in one direction only, half-duplex sends both ways but one direction at a time (walkie-talkies), and full-duplex sends both ways at the same moment (a phone call)
caption: Figure: simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex transmission between devices A and B

alt: Logic circuit for X = (A NAND B) AND (B XOR C): input B feeds both the NAND gate and the XOR gate, and their outputs P and Q enter an AND gate that gives X
caption: Figure: the circuit for X = (A NAND B) AND (B XOR C); input B is shared by two gates

alt: Logic circuit for X = (A OR B) AND NOT C: A and B enter an OR gate giving P, C enters a NOT gate giving Q, and P and Q enter an AND gate whose output is X
caption: Figure: the circuit for X = (A OR B) AND NOT C, with working signals P and Q

alt: The URL https://www.greenvalleyschool.ac.zw/notes/physics.html split into the protocol https, the domain name www.greenvalleyschool.ac.zw (where .zw is the country code for Zimbabwe) and the path and file name /notes/physics.html
caption: Figure: the protocol, domain name and path of a URL

alt: Von Neumann CPU: the PC holds the next address and passes it to the MAR, which sends it on the one-way address bus to RAM; the instruction returns on the two-way data bus into the MDR, then the CIR, where the control unit decodes it; the ALU puts results in the ACC
caption: Figure: the Von Neumann CPU with its registers, units and the three buses to RAM
